equation.name: The Evidence-to-Claim Decomposition
equation.latex: \text{Claim Validity} = \underbrace{\text{Measurement Fidelity}}_{\text{Physics \& Metadata}} \times \underbrace{\text{Transformation Contract}}_{\text{Invariants Preserved}} \times \underbrace{\text{Out-of-Sample Generalization}}_{\text{Independent Evaluation}}
equation.summary: Breaks any published neuroimaging conclusion into three multiplicative logical gates: if any single stage fails, the downstream claim collapses.

terms.meaning: Captures what the scanner physically recorded (TR, TE, voxel size, B0 field) versus what was lost before software ever touched the file.
terms.failure: Confusing BOLD T2* hemodynamic contrast with direct millisecond neuronal spiking.

terms.meaning: Specifies the exact domain, codomain, fitted parameters, preserved invariants, and destroyed degrees of freedom of the processing/modeling pipeline.
terms.failure: Applying a black-box script that silently alters coordinate frames or smooths across tissue boundaries.

terms.meaning: Tests whether the estimated effect or prediction survives on unseen participants and independent scanners without data leakage.
terms.failure: Reporting in-sample or circularly selected statistics as generalizable population truth.

online_diagram.title: The Scientific Cycle & Three-Pass Paper Forensics
online_diagram.guide: Notice how empirical measurement sits between a theoretical question and a falsifiable claim. In Pass 1–2 of reading a neuroimaging paper, map the main figure's axes, physical units, and transformation chain before reading the authors' narrative interpretation.

equation.name: Composite Spatial Preprocessing Operator
equation.latex: I_{\text{analysis}}(\mathbf{x}) = \left(\mathcal{R}_{\text{interp}} \circ T_{\text{MNI}\leftarrow\text{T1w}} \circ T_{\text{T1w}\leftarrow\text{EPI}} \circ T_{\text{SDC}} \circ T_{\text{motion}, t}\right)\!\big[I_{\text{raw}}(\mathbf{i}, t)\big]
equation.summary: Chains every spatial transformation into a single composite pullback mapping so voxel intensities are interpolated only once rather than blurred repeatedly.

terms.meaning: The discrete 4D integer/float array on the scanner's native voxel lattice i=(i,j,k) at frame t.
terms.failure: Treating raw voxel indices as matched anatomical locations across time or participants.

terms.meaning: 6-DOF head motion realignment composed with phase-encoding B0 susceptibility unwarping.
terms.failure: Ignoring residual spin-history and B0-by-motion interactions after rigid realignment.

terms.meaning: Boundary-based EPI-to-T1w registration composed with nonlinear diffeomorphic warp to standard template space.
terms.failure: Resampling after each individual step, which compounds interpolation smoothing.

terms.meaning: Evaluates the continuous interpolation kernel (Lanczos/B-spline for images, nearest-neighbor for integer labels) once on the target grid.
terms.failure: Using linear interpolation on discrete parcellation labels, inventing blended ROI integers.

online_diagram.title: From Scanner Acquisition to Standardized fMRI Workflow (fMRIPrep & BrainMorph)
online_diagram.guide: Raw functional and structural scans contain head motion, susceptibility warping, intensity bias, and arbitrary scanner coordinates. A transparent processing pipeline aligns anatomy and function while exposing visual quality-control checkpoints at every stage.

equation.name: Attenuated Out-of-Sample Brain-Wide Association Correlation
equation.summary: Shows why observed brain-behavior correlations are bounded by measurement reliability and why small-N studies suffer massive sampling dispersion.

terms.meaning: The true population correlation between the noiseless neural trait and the noiseless behavioral phenotype.
terms.failure: Assuming a small latent effect (e.g., r=0.10) will look large in a small sample without winner's curse inflation.

terms.meaning: Geometric mean of brain-measure test-retest reliability (ICC_X) and behavioral reliability (ICC_Y), shrinking the observable correlation.
terms.failure: Using noisy short-scan resting-state edges (low ICC_X) that cap observable correlation near zero.

terms.meaning: Sampling error of order O(1/sqrt(N)) that causes small samples (N=25) to produce wildly inflated or sign-reversed significant hits.
terms.failure: Thresholding small-N correlations at p<0.05, which guarantees high Type M (magnitude) and Type S (sign) errors.

online_diagram.title: Out-of-Sample Generalization & Cross-Validation Partitioning (Marek et al. & BrainIAC)
online_diagram.guide: In K-fold and multi-site cross-validation, every preprocessing parameter, feature screen, and model weight must be estimated strictly inside the training folds (blue) and evaluated once on held-out participants/sites (orange).

equation.name: Total Variance Across Analytical Pipelines (Multiverse Decomposition)
equation.latex: \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}) = \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\!\left[\operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta} \mid \pi)\right]}_{\text{Sampling Variance Within Pipeline}} + \underbrace{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi}\!\left(\mathbb{E}[\hat{\theta} \mid \pi]\right)}_{\text{Pipeline / Vibration Variance Across Choices}}
equation.summary: Decomposes total uncertainty into standard within-pipeline sampling error plus the hidden variance across defensible analysis pipelines.

terms.meaning: True total variance of the reported scientific estimate across both participant sampling and analytical branches.
terms.failure: Reporting only the first term and pretending the pipeline choice had zero impact.

terms.meaning: Average sampling variance printed by software assuming a single fixed pipeline pi.
terms.failure: Treating a narrow single-pipeline p-value as proof that the scientific conclusion is robust.

terms.meaning: Dispersion of the expected estimate across valid preprocessing, design, and inference specifications (NARPS).
terms.failure: Cherry-picking the single pipeline branch pi* that maximizes statistical significance.

online_diagram.title: Analytical Variability & Multiverse Evidence Audits (NARPS & Omni-fMRI)
online_diagram.guide: When 70 independent research teams analyze the exact same neuroimaging dataset (NARPS), legitimate variations in smoothing, motion modeling, and thresholding create a forest of divergent effect estimates. Auditing evidence requires separating data signal from researcher degrees of freedom.

equation.name: Explicit Transformation Contract Specification
equation.summary: Defines every neuroimaging code step as a typed mathematical mapping with explicit array dimensions, physical units, coordinate frame, and training-only fit scope.

terms.meaning: Input array with named axis dimensions (e.g., X,Y,Z,T), physical units (e.g., mm, s, arb. intensity), and coordinate space (e.g., native RAS+).
terms.failure: Passing unnamed NumPy arrays where voxel and time axes are silently transposed.

terms.meaning: Parameters (means, scalers, PCA axes, ComBat shifts, model weights) estimated strictly on the training partition.
terms.failure: Fitting parameters on the full dataset before splitting, causing data leakage.

terms.meaning: Transformed output whose shape, units, preserved invariants, and destroyed information are verified by assertions.
terms.failure: Accepting plausible-looking AI plots without checking numerical invariants.

online_diagram.title: The Human-AI Scientific Supervision Loop
online_diagram.guide: In agentic neuroimaging workflows, the AI coding assistant (Goose + Qwen) translates your explicit mathematical contract into executable code, while you (backed by Gemma 4 auditing and numerical assertions) verify invariants, axes, and physical units.

equation.name: Spoiled Gradient-Echo (GRE / EPI) Steady-State Signal Equation
equation.latex: S_{\text{GRE}}(\text{TR}, \text{TE}, \theta) \propto \underbrace{\rho}_{\text{Spin Density}} \cdot \underbrace{\frac{\sin\theta\left(1 - e^{-\text{TR}/T_1}\right)}{1 - \cos\theta\, e^{-\text{TR}/T_1}}}_{\text{Steady-State } T_1 \text{ \& Flip-Angle Gain}} \cdot \underbrace{e^{-\text{TE}/T_2^*}}_{\text{BOLD } T_2^* \text{ Dephasing Decay}}
equation.summary: Governs how sequence timing (TR, TE, flip angle theta) interacts with tissue relaxation (T1, T2*) to produce anatomical contrast and functional BOLD sensitivity.

terms.meaning: Baseline concentration of mobile 1H water/lipid spins setting the maximum available magnetization M0.
terms.failure: Mistaking raw voxel intensity for absolute proton density without accounting for T1, T2*, and coil bias.

terms.meaning: Determines how much longitudinal magnetization recovers between pulses spaced by TR and projects into the receiver plane via sin(theta); maximized at the Ernst angle arccos(e^{-TR/T1}).
terms.failure: Using a 90-degree flip angle at short TR, saturating long-T1 gray matter and CSF.

terms.meaning: Exponential signal attenuation over echo time TE driven by spin-spin relaxation (1/T2) plus local magnetic field inhomogeneities (gamma Delta B0 from paramagnetic deoxyhemoglobin).
terms.failure: Setting TE too short (no BOLD contrast) or too long (total susceptibility dropout near sinuses).

online_diagram.commons_title: File:Magnetization Relaxation Longitudinal Transversal T1 T2.png
online_diagram.title: Bloch Longitudinal (T1) Recovery & Transverse (T2 / T2*) Relaxation Curves
online_diagram.guide: Compare the rising longitudinal recovery curve M_z(t) = M_0(1 - e^{-t/T1}) against the decaying transverse coherence curve M_xy(t) = M_0 e^{-t/T2}. Repetition Time (TR) samples the T1 recovery curve; Echo Time (TE) samples the T2/T2* decay curve.

equation.name: Axis-Specific Protected z-Standardization
equation.latex: Z_{v, t} = \begin{cases} \dfrac{X_{v, t} - \mu_v}{\sigma_v} & \text{if } \sigma_v > \epsilon \\[6pt] 0 & \text{if } \sigma_v \le \epsilon \end{cases}, \qquad \mu_v = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} X_{v, t}, \quad \sigma_v = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T - \delta}\sum_{t=1}^{T}(X_{v, t} - \mu_v)^2}
equation.summary: Removes each voxel's static baseline offset and scales its temporal fluctuation to unit variance while guarding against out-of-brain zero-variance voxels.

terms.meaning: Subtracts voxel v's temporal mean across T time points so static T1/T2* baseline brightness is removed.
terms.failure: Computing X.mean(axis=0) across voxels instead of axis=1 across time, mixing anatomy with dynamics.

terms.meaning: Divides by the voxel's temporal standard deviation (population ddof=0 vs. sample ddof=1).
terms.failure: Leaving ddof unspecified when comparing code outputs against analytical formulas.

terms.meaning: Replaces 0/0 division in constant background masks with 0.0 instead of propagating NaN/Inf across the volume.
terms.failure: Allowing a single masked background voxel to poison downstream matrix multiplications with NaNs.

online_diagram.title: Auditing Code Snippets: Descriptive Standardization vs. Inferential Statistics
online_diagram.guide: Standardizing an array to mean 0 and standard deviation 1 rescales its units (horizontal axis), but does not change its distribution shape or compute a p-value. Auditing AI code requires reading every axis argument, degree-of-freedom flag (ddof), and division guard.

equation.name: Deterministic Computational State Transition
equation.summary: Formalizes a reproducible notebook as a pure composition of state transitions from a fixed random seed s0 and immutable input data.

terms.meaning: Each cell k must depend only on definitions executed in cells 1..k-1 in strict linear order.
terms.failure: Running Cell 8 before Cell 4 or deleting a cell whose variable still lingers in RAM.

terms.meaning: Input arrays are copied or treated as read-only rather than modified in-place across re-runs.
terms.failure: In-place operations like X -= X.mean() that change results when a cell is run twice.

terms.meaning: Local Generator instance np.random.default_rng(s0) supplying deterministic draws independent of global state.
terms.failure: Relying on unseeded global np.random calls that shift every time a cell is re-executed.

online_diagram.title: Deterministic Execution State & Hidden Kernel Mutation in Notebooks
online_diagram.guide: A Jupyter notebook is an interactive REPL with mutable global state in memory. Out-of-order cell execution, in-place array mutation, and unseeded random number generators destroy reproducibility unless verified in a clean top-to-bottom kernel.

equation.name: Boolean Mask Indexing & Stride-Aware Tensor Broadcasting
equation.latex: Y_{\text{masked}} = \mathcal{M}(Y_{X\times Y\times Z\times T}, M_{X\times Y\times Z}) \in \mathbb{R}^{V_{\text{brain}} \times T}, \qquad \text{offset}(i_0,\dots,i_{d-1}) = \sum_{k=0}^{d-1} s_k \, i_k
equation.summary: Maps a 4D volume through a 3D spatial mask into a 2D (V_brain, T) matrix and tracks byte stride offsets across array views.

terms.meaning: Boolean array selecting the V_brain = sum(M) in-brain voxels in a deterministic C-order traversal.
terms.failure: Flattening with Fortran order ('F') on mask extraction and C order ('C') on reconstruction, scrambling brain anatomy.

terms.meaning: Each row is one in-brain voxel's time series; each column is one volume across the brain mask.
terms.failure: Calling .reshape(T, V) instead of .T to transpose a (V, T) matrix, mixing time points across different voxels.

terms.meaning: Computes exact RAM address from index tuple i_k and byte strides s_k without copying array buffers.
terms.failure: Subtracting a 1D vector of length V from a (V, T) matrix without [:, None] or keepdims=True.

DS01.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: 4D Neuroimaging Tensor Axes, Memory Strides, Broadcasting & Boolean Brain Masks
online_diagram.guide: A 4D fMRI array has shape (X, Y, Z, T). Applying a 3D boolean brain mask M of shape (X, Y, Z) compresses the spatial dimensions into a 2D matrix X_masked of shape (V_brain, T). Confusing C-order reshape with transpose scrambles spatial and temporal axes!

equation.name: Relational Join Cardinality & Many-to-Many Cartesian Multiplication
equation.latex: |A \bowtie_{K} B| = \sum_{k \in K(A) \cap K(B)} n_A(k) \cdot n_B(k), \qquad \text{Valid } 1\text{:}m \iff \forall k, \; n_A(k) = 1
equation.summary: Proves why joining two tables that both have multiple rows per key k multiplies row counts to n_A(k) * n_B(k) unless constrained by a composite key.

terms.meaning: Uniquely identifies the observational unit across longitudinal visits and runs.
terms.failure: Joining longitudinal behavioral sessions to longitudinal MRI scans on participant_id alone, cross-pairing Baseline with Year-2 visits.

terms.meaning: If participant k has 3 sessions in table A and 3 scans in table B, an unkeyed join fabricates 3*3 = 9 rows for that person.
terms.failure: Omitting validate='one_to_one' or 'one_to_many' in pd.merge, silently duplicating clinical subjects.

terms.meaning: Subjects whose ID formatting ('sub-01' vs '01' vs 'sub-1 ') mismatches are silently dropped by an inner join.
terms.failure: Losing 20% of a cohort to trailing whitespace or zero-padding mismatches in subject IDs.

DS02.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Relational BIDS Tables, Composite Keys (sub + ses + run) & Many-to-Many Join Explosions
online_diagram.guide: Neuroimaging cohorts store demographics in participants.tsv (1 row per person), clinical visits in sessions.tsv (1 row per visit), and QC metrics per run. Joining two multi-row tables on participant_id alone—without session_id—creates a Cartesian many-to-many row explosion that duplicates participants!

pipeline_steps: Apply Header Scaling: m * Y_raw + b

equation.name: NIfTI Header Intensity Affine Scaling & Quantization Error Bound
equation.summary: Reconstructs physical floating-point voxel values from compact on-disk integer arrays via the NIfTI header slope and intercept.

terms.meaning: Unscaled integer or float voxel values stored on disk (accessed raw via img.dataobj.get_unscaled()).
terms.failure: Reading raw unscaled bytes directly while ignoring session-specific scl_slope variations across scanner runs.

terms.meaning: Applied automatically by img.get_fdata() to restore physical intensity or probability ranges.
terms.failure: Writing floating-point probability maps (0.0 to 1.0) into an integer NIfTI header with scl_slope=1, truncating all probabilities < 1 to 0!

terms.meaning: float32 provides 24 bits (~7 decimal digits) of significand precision; accumulating millions of voxel sums in float16/float32 can suffer catastrophic cancellation.
terms.failure: Using low-precision accumulators for whole-brain variance or Gram matrix calculations.

DS03.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: NIfTI-1 Binary File Contracts, IEEE-754 Floating-Point Precision & Header Scaling (scl_slope)
online_diagram.guide: A NIfTI file stores raw disk integers (e.g., int16) plus affine metadata (sform/qform) and intensity scaling factors (scl_slope, scl_inter). Casting float32/float64 statistical maps or high-dynamic-range signals to int16 without scaling truncates fractional values to zero!

pipeline_steps: Compare OLS vs. Huber Robust Fit

equation.name: Gaussian-Consistent Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) & Robust Z-Score
equation.summary: Estimates dispersion via the median distance from the median, scaled by 1 / Phi^{-1}(0.75) = 1.4826 to match standard deviation under a Gaussian distribution.

terms.meaning: Middle order statistic unaffected by extreme motion or hardware spike values in either tail.
terms.failure: Reporting only bar charts of sample means +/- SEM, which conceal bimodal site splits and extreme outliers.

terms.meaning: Multiplies raw MAD by 1/0.67449 = 1.4826 so it equals sigma when the bulk distribution is normal.
terms.failure: Using unscaled MAD as sigma, underestimating spread by ~33%, or using classical z = (x - mean)/sd where the outlier inflates sd and masks itself!

terms.meaning: Flags anomalous scans or ROI values without being swamped by the very outliers being detected.
terms.failure: Automatically deleting biological extremes (e.g., severe atrophy in a patient) without visual QC.

DS04.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), Heavy-Tailed Artifacts & Robust Summaries (Median / MAD / IQR)
online_diagram.guide: Neuroimaging quality metrics (FD, DVARS) and small-ROI summaries often contain extreme motion spikes or registration outliers. A single corrupted volume can shift the sample mean and explode the standard deviation (breakdown point 0%), whereas the median, IQR, and scaled MAD remain stable up to 50% contamination.

pipeline_steps: Test Association of R_i with Covariates
Split Train and Test Folds First

equation.name: Missingness Mechanism Taxonomy & Train-Only Imputation Boundary
equation.latex: P(R \mid Y_{\text{obs}}, Y_{\text{miss}}) = \begin{cases} P(R) & \text{MCAR} \\ P(R \mid Y_{\text{obs}}) & \text{MAR} \\ P(R \mid Y_{\text{obs}}, Y_{\text{miss}}) & \text{MNAR} \end{cases}, \qquad \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{imp}}^{(k)} = \operatorname{fit}\!\left(X_{\text{train}}^{(k)}\right)
equation.summary: Classifies missing data by whether drop-out depends on observed or unobserved values, and restricts imputer estimation to each training fold.

terms.meaning: Probability of missingness depends on observed variables (e.g., older or higher-motion subjects fail QC more often), recoverable via conditioning or IPW.
terms.failure: Treating MAR clinical dropout as MCAR complete-case data, biasing cohort estimates toward healthy low-motion subjects.

terms.meaning: Missingness depends directly on the unobserved value itself (e.g., severe cognitive impairment causing skipped cognitive tests); requires sensitivity bounds.
terms.failure: Assuming standard imputation cures MNAR selection bias without sensitivity analysis.

terms.meaning: Means, medians, or iterative regression weights fitted exclusively on fold k's training rows and applied to fold k's test rows.
terms.failure: Calling SimpleImputer().fit_transform(X_all) before cross-validation.

DS05.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Missingness Mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) & Fold-Isolated Train-Only Imputation
online_diagram.guide: When clinical covariates or regional imaging features have missing values, fitting an imputer on the entire dataset before cross-validation leaks test-fold distribution moments into training, and naïve mean imputation shrinks variance and distorts correlations.

pipeline_steps: Apply Bayes' Rule for PPV & NPV

equation.name: Bayes' Theorem for Positive Predictive Value (PPV) Under Low Base Rates
equation.latex: \text{PPV} = P(D^+ \mid T^+) = \frac{\overbrace{P(T^+ \mid D^+)}^{\text{Sensitivity}} \cdot \overbrace{\pi}^{\text{Prevalence}}}{\underbrace{P(T^+ \mid D^+)\,\pi}_{\text{True Positives}} + \underbrace{\big(1 - P(T^- \mid D^-)\big)(1 - \pi)}_{\text{False Positives}}}
equation.summary: Transforms test sensitivity and specificity into the actual posterior probability that a positive scan comes from a true case given population prevalence pi.

terms.meaning: Prior probability of the condition in the deployment population (often 1%–5% in population screening vs. 50% in balanced case-control studies).
terms.failure: Reporting balanced 50/50 case-control accuracy as if it were the predictive value in a real hospital clinic.

terms.meaning: Fraction of the total population that both has the disorder and tests positive.
terms.failure: Confusing sensitivity P(T+ | D+) with PPV P(D+ | T+) (the Prosecutor's / Reverse-Inference Fallacy).

terms.meaning: When prevalence pi is small, even a tiny false-positive rate (1 - Spec = 0.05) multiplied by the huge healthy majority (1 - pi = 0.99) overwhelms true positives.
terms.failure: Relying only on ROC-AUC under severe class imbalance instead of inspecting the Precision-Recall curve and PPV.

DS06.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Conditional Probability, Base-Rate Neglect, Positive Predictive Value (PPV) & ROC vs. PR Curves
online_diagram.guide: A neuroimaging classifier with 90% sensitivity and 90% specificity sounds accurate—until you apply it to a clinical screening population where disease prevalence is 1%: the Positive Predictive Value P(Disease | Positive Scan) is only ~8.3%! Always separate P(Data | Hypothesis) from P(Hypothesis | Data).

pipeline_steps: Measure Sample Size N & Autocorrelation rho
Compare Naive vs. Adjusted Confidence Intervals

equation.name: Autocorrelation-Adjusted Effective Sample Size & Standard Error
equation.summary: Reduces the nominal number of time points T by the integrated autocorrelation time to reflect the true number of independent degrees of freedom.

terms.meaning: Correlation between fMRI samples separated by k TRs; positive due to the sluggish ~6 s hemodynamic response.
terms.failure: Treating 1,000 multiband TRs (TR=0.5 s) as 1,000 independent draws when computing correlation p-values.

terms.meaning: At lag-1 autocorrelation rho_1 = 0.6, each TR provides only (0.4/1.6) = 25% of an independent observation!
terms.failure: Using unadjusted sqrt(T - 2) in Fisher-z standard errors 1/sqrt(T - 3), wildly inflating connectivity significance.

terms.meaning: Governs the actual width of the sampling distribution across repeated runs or participants.
terms.failure: Confusing the standard deviation of the data (sigma) with the standard error of the mean (SE).

DS07.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Sampling Distributions, Temporal Autocorrelation & Effective Sample Size (N_eff)
online_diagram.guide: The standard error of a mean shrinks as sigma / sqrt(N) only when observations are independent. In fMRI time series with positive autocorrelation rho_1, adjacent TRs carry redundant information, shrinking the effective sample size N_eff and widening the true sampling distribution.

pipeline_steps: Include All Runs/Rows of Selected Participants
Recompute Estimator theta-hat*_b on Each Resample

equation.name: Participant-Level Cluster Bootstrap Resampling & Percentile Interval
equation.summary: Resamples complete participant data blocks with replacement to preserve within-participant covariance across runs, time points, and brain regions.

terms.meaning: Draws N participant IDs with replacement (~63.2% unique participants per bootstrap replicate).
terms.failure: Resampling individual fMRI volumes or multi-run table rows independently, destroying within-subject dependence and narrowing CIs.

terms.meaning: Carries all runs, visits, and voxels of chosen participant i_m together into replicate b.
terms.failure: Using bootstrap replicates as a cross-validation split (where duplicates appear in both train and test sets!).

terms.meaning: Spans the central (1 - alpha) quantiles of the B bootstrap estimates without parametric normality assumptions.
terms.failure: Running too few bootstrap replicates (e.g., B=50 instead of B>=1,000–5,000) for tail quantile stability.

DS08.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Nonparametric Bootstrap Uncertainty & Cluster Resampling at the Participant Unit
online_diagram.guide: Bootstrapping estimates sampling uncertainty by drawing B resamples with replacement of size N. In hierarchical neuroimaging data (multiple runs, trials, or parcels per person), you MUST resample whole participants (cluster bootstrap) rather than individual rows!

equation.name: Average Treatment Effect (ATE) & Backdoor Adjustment Formula
equation.latex: \tau_{\text{ATE}} = \mathbb{E}\!\big[Y_i(1) - Y_i(0)\big] = \sum_{z} \Big(\mathbb{E}[Y \mid A=1, Z=z] - \mathbb{E}[Y \mid A=0, Z=z]\Big) P(Z=z)
equation.summary: Links the unobservable counterfactual causal estimand to observable conditional expectations when all backdoor confounding paths Z are blocked.

terms.meaning: Difference between participant i's brain outcome under exposure A=1 versus A=0; only one potential outcome is ever observed per person at a fixed time.
terms.failure: Jumping straight to a software button (e.g., 'run two-sample t-test') without defining the causal or descriptive target estimand.

terms.meaning: Variables (e.g., age, scanner site, head motion tendency) that cause both exposure A and brain outcome Y and must be adjusted for.
terms.failure: Conditioning on a collider C (A -> C <- Y, e.g., hospital admission or QC selection driven by both disease and scan quality), inducing spurious association.

terms.meaning: Averages stratum-specific differences over the marginal distribution of Z in the target population.
terms.failure: Interpreting observational neuroimaging correlations as causal intervention effects when unmeasured confounders remain open.

D01.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Causal Estimands, Potential Outcomes & Confounder vs. Mediator vs. Collider Structure
online_diagram.guide: Before choosing a statistical test, state the scientific question as a formal estimand: the target population, the exposure/contrast, the unit of analysis, and the causal graph. Adjusting for a common-cause confounder Z removes bias, whereas conditioning on a post-treatment mediator M or common-effect collider C creates bias!

equation.name: Horvitz-Thompson Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) & Design Effect
equation.summary: Reweights retained participants (R_i=1) by the inverse of their retention probability pi(X_i) under MAR and adjusts effective sample size for within-participant clustering.

terms.meaning: Equals 1 if participant i's scan survives acquisition and motion QC, and 0 if missing/excluded.
terms.failure: Assuming complete-case analysis is unbiased when motion exclusion (R_i=0) correlates with age or clinical symptom severity.

terms.meaning: Upweights retained participants from demographic/clinical strata X_i that had higher exclusion rates, restoring target-population balance under MAR.
terms.failure: Ignoring extreme propensity weights near zero without stabilization or positivity checks.

terms.meaning: Factor by which m repeated scans/rows per person inflate variance when within-person correlation rho_ICC > 0.
terms.failure: Running df = N*m - 2 across all rows as if 4 runs from 20 people were 80 independent humans.

D02.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Sampling Frames, Missingness Mechanisms (MCAR / MAR / MNAR) & Participant vs. Row Units
online_diagram.guide: Neuroimaging tables often contain multiple rows per participant (runs, visits, parcels). Treating rows as independent participants inflates sample size, and dropping participants who fail motion QC alters the target population unless missingness is properly weighted.

pipeline_steps: Define Baseline Reference B_v (Mean vs. Rest)
Verify Effect on Group GLM Betas

equation.name: Percent Signal Change (PSC) vs. Temporal z-Standardization
equation.summary: Contrasts baseline-normalized percentage units against variance-normalized z-units whose denominator depends on both task amplitude and scanner noise.

terms.meaning: Voxel v's temporal mean (or explicit pre-stimulus rest baseline) representing equilibrium T2* signal intensity.
terms.failure: Computing PSC after mean-centering the time series (where B_v = 0!), causing division by zero.

terms.meaning: Expresses BOLD fluctuations as a percentage of local baseline intensity (typically 0.5%–3.0% in cortex at 3T).
terms.failure: Dividing by tiny out-of-brain or sinus-dropout baselines without a brain mask guard, creating +5000% edge spikes.

terms.meaning: Temporal z-scoring divides by total temporal SD; therefore a voxel with huge task activation increases its own denominator and self-attenuates its beta!
terms.failure: Interpreting z-scored GLM betas as pure response amplitudes when thermal noise varies across coils or groups.

DS09.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Temporal z-Standardization vs. Percent Signal Change (PSC) & Baseline Reference Choices
online_diagram.guide: Raw fMRI scanner units are arbitrary. Converting a voxel time series to Percent Signal Change (PSC = 100 * (Y_t - B_v) / B_v) preserves interpretable physiological magnitude (~1–3% BOLD change), whereas temporal z-scoring divides by the voxel's total temporal SD (which mixes task signal and noise variance!).

pipeline_steps: Inspect Singular Values sigma_i of X
Compute Orthogonal Projector P_X = X X^+

equation.name: Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse Projection & Contrast Estimability Condition
equation.latex: \hat{\mathbf{y}} = P_{\mathcal{C}(X)}\,\mathbf{y} = X X^{+} \mathbf{y}, \qquad \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = X^{+}\mathbf{y} + \left(I_p - X^{+}X\right)\mathbf{w}, \qquad \mathbf{c}^T\boldsymbol{\beta} \text{ is estimable} \iff \mathbf{c} \in \mathcal{R}(X^T)
equation.summary: Shows that while fitted values y-hat are always unique, parameter vector beta has an arbitrary nullspace component (I - X^+ X)w whenever columns of X are linearly dependent.

terms.meaning: Symmetric idempotent matrix (P^2 = P, P^T = P) projecting y orthogonally onto the subspace spanned by columns of X.
terms.failure: Calling np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X) on a rank-deficient design matrix, raising LinAlgError or exploding to 1e16.

terms.meaning: When a regressor equals the sum of two other regressors (e.g., Intercept + Dummy_A + Dummy_B), infinitely many beta vectors yield the exact same fit y-hat.
terms.failure: Interpreting individual coefficients from a rank-deficient design where np.linalg.lstsq arbitrarily picks the minimum-norm solution.

terms.meaning: A linear contrast c^T beta is invariant to nullspace ambiguity if and only if c lies entirely in the row space of X.
terms.failure: Testing a non-estimable contrast that depends on how redundant columns were parameterized.

DS10.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Linear Algebra of Design Matrices: Column Space Projection, Rank Deficiency & Identifiability
online_diagram.guide: In linear regression y = X beta + e, the fitted signal y-hat = P_X y is unique because the orthogonal projection matrix P_X = X X^+ depends only on the column space C(X). However, the individual parameter vector beta-hat is uniquely identifiable if and only if X has full column rank (rank(X) == p)!

pipeline_steps: Specify Parametric Likelihood p(y | X, theta)
Compare AIC / BIC Across Noise Models

equation.name: Equivalence of Negative Log-Likelihood and Loss Minimization
equation.summary: Unifies regression and classification losses as negative log-likelihoods under explicit data-generating noise distributions.

terms.meaning: Converts a product of tiny probabilities (which underflows float64 to 0.0) into a numerically stable sum of log-probabilities.
terms.failure: Multiplying raw likelihoods prod_i p(y_i) across N=500 subjects, causing immediate floating-point underflow to 0.0.

terms.meaning: Gaussian L2 squares large residuals (optimal for thermal noise, fragile to spikes); Laplace L1 grows linearly (robust to outlier scans).
terms.failure: Using Gaussian OLS on spike-contaminated or skewed count data without checking residual normality.

terms.meaning: Raw MLE divides by N and underestimates variance when p parameters are fitted; REML/OLS divides by N - p.
terms.failure: Ignoring parameter degrees of freedom p when estimating residual variance in high-dimensional designs.

DS11.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE): Choosing the Noise Distribution Before Fitting
online_diagram.guide: Every loss function is a disguised probability model: minimizing squared error (OLS) is Maximum Likelihood under Gaussian noise, minimizing absolute error (L1) is MLE under heavy-tailed Laplace noise, and binary cross-entropy is MLE under a Bernoulli likelihood.

pipeline_steps: Verify Analytic Gradient vs. Finite Differences
Monitor Both Train Loss & Validation Generalization

equation.name: Gradient Descent Update & Largest-Eigenvalue Stability Bound
equation.summary: Steps opposite the gradient with learning rate eta bounded by the inverse of the largest Hessian curvature eigenvalue.

terms.meaning: Moves parameters in the direction of steepest local decrease of the training objective.
terms.failure: Getting trapped in a bad local minimum during 3D image registration when starting far from overlap without multi-resolution pyramids.

terms.meaning: If learning rate eta exceeds 2 / lambda_max, updates overshoot the valley walls with growing amplitude and explode to NaN/Inf.
terms.failure: Leaving raw unscaled covariates (e.g., TIV in 1,500,000 mm^3 alongside age in years), which explodes lambda_max and causes divergence.

terms.meaning: Driving training loss to zero only proves the optimizer worked; validation loss reveals when the model starts memorizing noise.
terms.failure: Equating a low training loss with a scientifically valid or generalizable model.

DS12.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Gradient-Based Optimization, Lipschitz Learning-Rate Bounds, Conditioning & Early Stopping
online_diagram.guide: Registration, deep learning, and regularized GLMs minimize an objective L(theta) iteratively along the negative gradient -grad L. If features have wildly different scales, the Hessian eigenvalues stretch into a narrow canyon (high condition number kappa), causing gradient descent to zig-zag or diverge unless features are standardized or preconditioned!

pipeline_steps: Compute ICC(3,1) Consistency vs. ICC(2,1) Agreement

equation.name: Intraclass Correlation Coefficient: Consistency ICC(3,1) vs. Absolute Agreement ICC(2,1)
equation.summary: Expresses individual-difference reliability as the fraction of total measurement variance attributable to true stable differences between people.

terms.meaning: Variance of stable trait levels across individuals in the population; must be large for a biomarker to rank people reliably.
terms.failure: Assuming a task with a huge group t-statistic automatically has high individual-difference reliability (the Reliability Paradox).

terms.meaning: Global offset between Session 1 and Session 2 (e.g., scanner upgrade or habituation); penalized by ICC(2,1) agreement but ignored by Pearson r and ICC(3,1).
terms.failure: Using Pearson r to claim longitudinal measurement equivalence when Session 2 is systematically shifted.

terms.meaning: Participant-by-session interaction plus thermal/physiological scan noise; shrinks by 1/k when averaging k repeat sessions in ICC(2,k).
terms.failure: Entering low-ICC contrast scores (ICC < 0.4) into small-sample brain-behavior correlations.

D03.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Test-Retest Reliability, Intraclass Correlation (ICC) & Group vs. Individual Paradox
online_diagram.guide: A robust group-level task effect (e.g., Stroop or Flanker activation) occurs when within-subject differences are consistent across everyone (small between-subject variance sigma_B^2). Paradoxically, that same low between-subject variance makes the measure unreliable for ranking individual differences (low ICC; Hedge et al., 2018)!

pipeline_steps: Evaluate Power 1 - beta at Stringent alpha
Audit Type M Exaggeration & Type S Sign Error
Plan Sample Size for CI Half-Width w

equation.name: Noncentral-t Power, Winner's Curse Exaggeration (Type M) & Precision Sample Size
equation.latex: \lambda = d_{\text{obs}}\sqrt{N_{\text{eff}}}, \qquad \text{Type M} = \frac{\mathbb{E}\!\left[|\hat{d}| \;\middle|\; |T| > t_{1-\alpha/2}\right]}{|d_{\text{true}}|} \gg 1 \text{ when Power is low}, \qquad N_{\text{CI}} \ge \left(\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}\,\sigma}{w}\right)^2
equation.summary: Connects sample size and effect size to the noncentrality parameter lambda, explains why significant hits in underpowered studies overestimate true effects, and sizes studies for confidence-interval width.

terms.meaning: Ratio of true (reliability-attenuated) effect size to standard error; governs the shift of the alternative t-distribution.
terms.failure: Plugging an inflated pilot-study effect size (d=0.9 from N=20) into a power calculator.

terms.meaning: Conditioning on crossing a strict significance threshold truncates the sampling distribution to its outer tails, inflating observed effects by 2x–5x at low power.
terms.failure: Interpreting a significant p<0.001 voxel in N=25 as proof that the true population effect is large.

terms.meaning: Sample size required to guarantee that the 95% confidence interval half-width does not exceed a scientifically tolerable margin w.
terms.failure: Planning for alpha=0.05 single-test power when the real analysis tests 50,000 voxels or edges.

D04.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Statistical Power, Precision Planning & The Winner's Curse (Type M and Type S Errors)
online_diagram.guide: When statistical power is low (e.g., 15–20% in small-N neuroimaging studies), the few results that cross the p < 0.05 significance threshold are guaranteed by conditional truncation to have massively exaggerated effect sizes (Type M error / Winner's Curse) and an elevated risk of having the wrong sign (Type S error)!

equation.name: Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) & Cook's Distance Influence Metric
equation.summary: Quantifies how much predictor j's variance is inflated by correlation with other predictors (VIF) and how strongly observation i pulls the fitted parameter vector (Cook's D_i).

terms.meaning: Factor by which Var(beta-hat_j) is multiplied compared to an orthogonal design; VIF > 5–10 signals severe instability.
terms.failure: Entering both global brain volume and sum of left+right hemisphere volumes into the same OLS model.

terms.meaning: Measures how far participant i's predictors sit from the sample centroid; bounded in [1/N, 1] with sum(h_ii) = p.
terms.failure: Checking only vertical residual size e_i while missing an extreme leverage point that pulled the line straight through itself (small e_i, huge h_ii)!

terms.meaning: Combines residual magnitude and leverage to measure how much all fitted values shift if participant i is removed.
terms.failure: Publishing a brain-behavior correlation driven entirely by 1–2 high-Cook's-distance subjects.

DS13.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.commons_title: File:Effect of multicollinearity on coefficients of linear model.png
online_diagram.title: Regression Diagnostics: Collinearity (VIF), High-Leverage Points & Cook's Distance
online_diagram.guide: Even when a regression model has a high overall R^2, near-collinear predictors (high Variance Inflation Factor, VIF) make individual beta weights wildly unstable and sign-flip across samples, while a single high-leverage participant (high hat-value h_{ii} and Cook's distance D_i) can dictate the entire regression line.

pipeline_steps: Center Columns Using Train Mean mu_train
Compute Economy SVD: X_c = U S V^T
Project Test Data: Z_test = (X_test - mu_train) V_K

equation.name: Centered Singular Value Decomposition & Out-of-Sample PCA Projection
equation.latex: X_{\text{train}, c} = U \Sigma V^T, \qquad \lambda_k = \frac{\sigma_k^2}{N_{\text{train}} - 1}, \qquad Z_{\text{test}} = \left(X_{\text{test}} - \mathbf{1}\hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\text{train}}^T\right) V_{(:, 1:K)}
equation.summary: Decomposes centered training data into orthogonal singular vectors and projects held-out test data onto the frozen top-K training axes V_K.

terms.meaning: Subtracts the training-fold feature mean before SVD so PC1 captures covariance around the centroid rather than the origin offset.
terms.failure: Running SVD on uncentered raw MRI intensities, where PC1 merely points from zero to the grand mean image.

terms.meaning: Proportion of total Frobenius energy captured by orthogonal axis k; high variance does NOT guarantee biological relevance over artifact.
terms.failure: Assuming '90% variance explained' means task or clinical signal was preserved when the top PCs are scanner drift and motion.

terms.meaning: Orthonormal loading vectors estimated strictly on X_train (note that each column v_k has arbitrary +/-1 sign indeterminacy across folds).
terms.failure: Fitting PCA on the combined train+test matrix before splitting, or comparing raw PC signs across folds without Procrustes alignment.

DS14.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), Principal Component Analysis (PCA) & Train-Only Basis Fitting
online_diagram.guide: SVD factors a centered data matrix X_c = U S V^T into orthogonal sample scores (U S) and principal spatial patterns (V). Because PCA is purely variance-maximizing, high-variance head motion or site offsets will dominate PC1 unless cleaned—and fitting V on the full dataset before cross-validation leaks test-fold covariance structure.

pipeline_steps: Generate Pure Null Test Case (X_null, y_null)
Move Feature Selector Inside CV Loop
Fit Screen + Model Strictly on X_train^(k)
Verify Permutation Null Centers at Chance (50% / r=0)

equation.name: Nested Within-Fold Feature Screening vs. Leaky Global Screening
equation.summary: Re-estimates the selected feature subset S^(k) from scratch inside every training fold k without ever consulting test-fold labels y_test^(k).

terms.meaning: Indices of the K features showing strongest association with y_train inside training fold k only.
terms.failure: Screening features once on (X_all, y_all) before cross-validation—the single most common fatal leakage bug in neuroimaging ML!

terms.meaning: Among P=50,000 pure noise edges and N=60 subjects, the maximum sample correlation E[max_j |r_j|] exceeds 0.50 by chance alone.
terms.failure: Trusting high in-sample correlations or leaky CV scores without running a full-pipeline label-permutation test.

terms.meaning: Measures overlap of selected edges across folds; low overlap reveals that multiple collinear edges trade places across splits.
terms.failure: Over-interpreting the exact biological identity of 10 unstable Lasso/screened edges when 500 correlated edges carry the same information.

DS15.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: High-Dimensional Feature Screening (P >> N) & Global vs. Fold-Isolated Selection Leakage
online_diagram.guide: In connectomics and voxelwise decoding, features P (10,000–100,000) vastly outnumber participants N (50–200). If you screen the 'top K most correlated edges' across all N participants before running K-fold cross-validation, a pure random-noise dataset will achieve >85% 'cross-validated accuracy'!

equation.name: End-to-End Reproducibility Contract & Audit Verification Function
equation.summary: Binds input data hashes, locked dependency versions, random seeds, split boundaries, and output artifact digests into a verifiable provenance record.

terms.meaning: Guarantees that the exact same input bytes and library versions (NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, NiBabel) are used.
terms.failure: Using unpinned pip install commands or mutating input files in place without version hashes.

terms.meaning: Asserts programmatic disjointness of participant and site IDs between training and evaluation sets.
terms.failure: Relying on AI-generated pipeline code without programmatically asserting zero participant overlap across splits.

terms.meaning: Executes assertions on shapes, units, null-permutation baselines, and expected numerical outcome ranges.
terms.failure: Accepting an AI-written analysis because the code ran without throwing a Python exception.

DS16.phase: Phase II · Neuroimaging Data Science & Experimental Foundations

online_diagram.title: End-to-End Computational Reproducibility, Cryptographic Manifests & AI Analysis Auditing
online_diagram.guide: A computational result is reproducible only when an independent researcher (or automated CI runner) can regenerate the exact numerical tables and figures from raw inputs using a locked environment (uv.lock), fixed seeds, and a cryptographic audit manifest.

pipeline_steps: Rotation R · Scaling S · Shear K
Physical World Space (x, y, z mm)

equation.name: NIfTI Homogeneous Voxel-to-World Affine Transformation
equation.latex: \begin{bmatrix} x_{\text{R}} \\ y_{\text{A}} \\ z_{\text{S}} \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} M_{3\times 3} & \mathbf{t}_{3\times 1} \\ \mathbf{0}^T & 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{A \text{ (4}\times\text{4 Affine)}} \begin{bmatrix} i \\ j \\ k \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \underbrace{(R \, S \, K)}_{\text{Linear Submatrix } M}\mathbf{i} + \underbrace{\mathbf{t}}_{\text{Origin Offset}}
equation.summary: Maps discrete array indices (i,j,k) to continuous physical coordinates (x,y,z) in millimeters in the scanner's RAS+ coordinate frame.

terms.meaning: Zero-based integer array subscripts along the three storage axes, augmented with 1 to enable translation via matrix multiplication.
terms.failure: Assuming axis 0 is always Left-to-Right without checking the affine matrix.

terms.meaning: 3x3 linear matrix encoding orthogonal slice rotation R, voxel spacing S=diag(di,dj,dk), and oblique gantry shear K; |det(M)| is voxel volume in mm^3.
terms.failure: Flipping an image array with np.flip without updating M, silently swapping Left and Right hemispheres.

terms.meaning: World RAS+ coordinates (in mm) of the center of corner voxel (0,0,0).
terms.failure: Constructing nib.Nifti1Image(data, np.eye(4)), which resets voxel spacing to 1mm and shifts the origin to (0,0,0).

PR01.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.commons_title: File:Human brain anatomical planes letter annotations.jpg
online_diagram.title: Anatomical Coordinate Planes (Axial, Coronal, Sagittal) & RAS+ Voxel-to-World Mapping
online_diagram.guide: A NIfTI file stores a 3D/4D grid of numbers (i, j, k) whose physical orientation in millimeters (Right-Anterior-Superior, RAS+) exists only through the 4x4 homogeneous affine matrix A in the header.

equation.name: Pullback (Backward) Image Resampling & Interpolation
equation.summary: Evaluates every voxel of the output grid by pulling coordinates backward into the moving image and convolving with an interpolation kernel psi.

terms.meaning: Maps each regular grid point x_m in fixed space back to its source location in moving space so no output voxel is left with holes.
terms.failure: Applying the forward transform instead of the inverse, moving the brain in the opposite direction or leaving unvisited grid holes.

terms.meaning: Converts continuous physical coordinates in moving space into fractional moving-array indices.
terms.failure: Mixing millimeter translations with voxel-index offsets when grids have different resolutions.

terms.meaning: Weights neighboring discrete samples (order 0 nearest-neighbor for integer masks/atlases; order 1–3 linear/B-spline for continuous intensities).
terms.failure: Using trilinear interpolation (order=1) on an integer parcellation atlas, creating invalid intermediate label IDs at region borders.

PR02.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Pullback Resampling & Continuous Interpolation on Discrete Grids
online_diagram.guide: When registering a moving image to a fixed target grid, we iterate over each target voxel center x_m, project it backward into the moving image via the inverse transform T^{-1}(x_m), and interpolate surrounding moving voxel intensities.

equation.name: Deformation Field & Local Jacobian Volume Change
equation.summary: Quantifies the local volumetric scaling factor induced by a nonlinear warp and certifies whether the transformation is a topology-preserving diffeomorphism.

terms.meaning: 3D vector at every voxel specifying the local millimeter shift from template space to native anatomy.
terms.failure: Over-penalizing or under-penalizing bending energy, leading to either residual misregistration or unphysical grid tearing.

terms.meaning: First-order linearization of the warp combining the identity matrix with spatial partial derivatives of the displacement.
terms.failure: Computing finite differences without dividing by physical voxel spacing (mm).

terms.meaning: Ratio of deformed elemental volume to original volume: J=1 preserves volume, J>1 expands, 0<J<1 compresses, and J<=0 indicates non-invertible folding.
terms.failure: Accepting a nonlinear registration without checking min(J) > 0 across the brain mask.

PR03.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Nonlinear Deformation Fields, Diffeomorphisms & Jacobian Determinant Folding Checks
online_diagram.guide: A nonlinear warp bends a coordinate grid locally via a displacement field u(x). The Jacobian determinant J(x) = det(I + grad u(x)) measures local volume expansion (J > 1) or compression (0 < J < 1); if J(x) <= 0, the grid has folded over itself and destroyed anatomical topology.

equation.name: Multiplicative Bias Field Model & Log-Domain N4 Decomposition
equation.latex: I_{\text{obs}}(\mathbf{x}) = B(\mathbf{x}) \cdot I_{\text{true}}(\mathbf{x}) + \eta(\mathbf{x}) \;\xrightarrow{\;\ln\;}\; \ln I_{\text{obs}}(\mathbf{x}) \approx \ln I_{\text{true}}(\mathbf{x}) + \ln B(\mathbf{x})
equation.summary: Converts a spatially varying multiplicative coil gain B(x) into an additive low-frequency offset in log-space that can be estimated with smooth B-splines.

terms.meaning: Spatially slowly varying RF reception/transmission sensitivity field that scales both tissue means and within-tissue variances.
terms.failure: Attempting additive background subtraction instead of multiplicative division.

terms.meaning: Logarithmic transform turns multiplication into addition so low-frequency B-spline smoothing isolates ln B(x).
terms.failure: Taking log(I_obs) without clamping zero/negative background noise voxels above epsilon.

terms.meaning: Divides out the smooth bias estimate to sharpen white/gray matter histogram peaks prior to tissue segmentation.
terms.failure: Using an overly flexible spline knot spacing that erases true biological focal lesions or cortical contrast.

PR04.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: RF Coil Sensitivity Shading & Multiplicative Bias Field Correction (N4ITK)
online_diagram.guide: Phased-array receiver coils and B1+ RF inhomogeneity multiply the true tissue contrast by a smooth spatial shading field B(x). Because the bias is multiplicative, a single tissue class (e.g., white matter) spans different intensity ranges across the brain until corrected in log-space.

equation.name: Sørensen–Dice Overlap vs. Directed Hausdorff Boundary Distance
equation.summary: Pairs a bulk volumetric overlap ratio (Dice) with a worst-case millimeter boundary excursion metric (Hausdorff distance).

terms.meaning: Harmonic mean of sensitivity and precision over interior brain voxels; dominated by the large deep brain core.
terms.failure: Relying solely on DSC, which remains ~0.97 even when 3 mm of superior parietal cortex is shaved off.

terms.meaning: Boundary voxel sets where pial gray matter meets CSF, dura, and skull.
terms.failure: Including bright neck fat or optic nerves that pull downstream registration off-target.

terms.meaning: Maximum Euclidean distance in millimeters from any point on one mask boundary to the closest point on the other.
terms.failure: Computing boundary distances in raw voxel counts instead of physical millimeters.

PR05.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Brain Extraction (Skull Stripping) & Boundary Distance Metrics (Dice vs. Hausdorff)
online_diagram.guide: A brain mask defines the computational universe for registration, bias correction, and statistical testing. High overall Dice overlap (>0.95) can still hide localized dural inclusions or cortical over-stripping that only surface boundary metrics (Hausdorff Distance, ASSD) detect.

pipeline_steps: Soft Partial-Volume Maps vs. Hard Labels

equation.name: Bayes Posterior Tissue Responsibility (EM E-Step)
equation.latex: \gamma_{ic} = P(Z_i = c \mid y_i, \boldsymbol{\Theta}) = \frac{\overbrace{\pi_c}^{\text{Prior}} \, \overbrace{\mathcal{N}(y_i \mid \mu_c, \sigma_c^2)}^{\text{Intensity Likelihood}}}{\underbrace{\sum_{k \in \{\text{CSF,GM,WM}\}} \pi_k \, \mathcal{N}(y_i \mid \mu_k, \sigma_k^2)}_{\text{Marginal Evidence at Voxel } i}}
equation.summary: Computes the continuous posterior probability that voxel i belongs to tissue class c by weighting its Gaussian intensity likelihood by the class prior.

terms.meaning: Prior probability of tissue class c (from global mixing proportions or a tissue probability atlas / MRF neighborhood).
terms.failure: Using flat priors on low-contrast scans where deep gray nuclei overlap white matter intensities.

terms.meaning: Gaussian density of observing voxel intensity y_i given tissue class mean mu_c and variance sigma_c^2.
terms.failure: Fitting GMMs before N4 bias correction, causing shaded white matter to be misclassified as gray matter.

terms.meaning: Continuous tissue responsibility summed across voxels to estimate unbiased partial-volume tissue volume.
terms.failure: Thresholding gamma_ic via argmax (hard labels), which systematically biases volume estimates in thin cortical ribbons.

PR06.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) Expectation-Maximization & Partial Volume Tissue Posteriors
online_diagram.guide: Instead of forcing every boundary voxel into a binary integer label, probabilistic tissue segmentation models the intensity histogram as a mixture of CSF, Gray Matter, and White Matter Gaussians coupled with a spatial Markov Random Field prior.

equation.name: Jacobian-Modulated Tissue Density & TIV Allometric Residualization
equation.latex: p_{\text{mod}}(\mathbf{x}) = \underbrace{p_{\text{nat}}\!\big(\boldsymbol{\phi}(\mathbf{x})\big)}_{\text{Unmodulated Tissue Concentration}} \cdot \underbrace{\big|\det(\nabla\boldsymbol{\phi}(\mathbf{x}))\big|}_{\text{Local Jacobian Volume Factor } J(\mathbf{x})}, \qquad V_{\text{adj}, i} = V_i - \hat{\beta}_{\text{TIV}}\!\left(\text{TIV}_i - \overline{\text{TIV}}\right)
equation.summary: Preserves native tissue volume (mm^3) after spatial normalization via Jacobian modulation, then adjusts regional volume for global head size (TIV).

terms.meaning: Resampled tissue probability at template coordinate x; reflects local concentration but loses native size differences.
terms.failure: Interpreting unmodulated VBM maps as regional gray matter volume (mm^3) rather than concentration.

terms.meaning: Scales template voxels up if native tissue was compressed into a smaller template region, ensuring integral(p_mod) equals native volume.
terms.failure: Modulating by 1/J(x) instead of J(x), which inverts atrophy into apparent hypertrophy.

terms.meaning: Removes linear scaling with Total Intracranial Volume (estimated on the reference group) before testing group atrophy.
terms.failure: Dividing crudely by TIV when scaling is non-proportional, or failing to account for sex-by-TIV collinearity.

PR07.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), Jacobian Modulation & Total Intracranial Volume (TIV) Adjustment
online_diagram.guide: Nonlinear registration warps every participant's brain to match the template's shape. Without multiplying the warped tissue map by the Jacobian determinant J(x) (modulation), regional volume differences are erased by the warp itself.

equation.name: Euler-Poincaré Topological Invariant & Symmetric Cortical Thickness
equation.summary: Enforces that each cortical hemisphere mesh is topologically equivalent to a hole-free sphere (genus g=0, Euler characteristic chi=2) before measuring vertex-wise cortical thickness.

terms.meaning: Alternating sum of mesh vertices, edges, and triangular faces; equals exactly 2 for any closed surface without handles or bridges (genus g=0).
terms.failure: Skipping topological defect correction, leaving segmentation handles/holes that corrupt spherical registration.

terms.meaning: Euclidean distance in mm from white-surface vertex w_v to the nearest point on the pial surface (not merely along one voxel axis).
terms.failure: Measuring thickness by counting voxels along a single grid axis, which overestimates thickness in obliquely tilted sulci.

terms.meaning: Surface-constrained geodesic path travels around the fundus of a sulcus rather than jumping across the 2 mm CSF gap between opposing gyral banks.
terms.failure: Applying 3D volumetric Gaussian smoothing that blends functional signals from opposing sulcal walls.

PR08.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Cortical Surface Meshes, Euler Characteristic Topology & Geodesic vs. Euclidean Distance
online_diagram.guide: The cerebral cortex is a folded 2D sheet (~2.5 mm thick). Representing it as a genus-0 triangular mesh (white and pial surfaces inflated to a sphere) prevents smoothing across sulcal CSF banks that are close in 3D Euclidean space but centimeters apart along the cortical sheet.

pipeline_steps: Sinc / Fourier Phase Shift in Time

equation.name: Fourier Phase-Shift Slice-Timing Correction
equation.latex: x_{\text{corr}}(z, t) = \mathcal{F}^{-1}\!\left\{\mathcal{F}\{x(z, t)\}(\omega) \cdot \underbrace{e^{+i \omega \Delta t_z}}_{\text{Linear Phase Shift}}\right\}, \qquad \Delta t_z = t_z - t_{\text{ref}}, \quad |\omega| \le \frac{\pi}{\text{TR}}
equation.summary: Shifts slice z's time series by its exact acquisition offset Delta t_z using the Fourier shift theorem within the Nyquist band.

terms.meaning: Signed delay (in seconds) between when slice z was physically excited and the chosen volume reference time t_ref.
terms.failure: Guessing sequential vs. interleaved slice order instead of reading the BIDS SliceTiming JSON array, or applying the shift with the wrong sign.

terms.meaning: Pure phase rotation proportional to angular frequency omega that shifts a bandlimited signal in time without attenuating its amplitude.
terms.failure: Applying slice-timing correction BEFORE motion realignment when large head movements shift tissue across slices.

terms.meaning: Maximum temporal frequency representable at sampling interval TR; rapid motion spikes violate bandlimitedness and cause temporal ringing.
terms.failure: Ignoring temporal derivatives in the GLM when long TRs (>2 s) leave residual slice-timing phase errors.

PR09.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Slice-Timing Acquisition Offsets & Temporal Phase Interpolation
online_diagram.guide: A 2D echo-planar fMRI volume is not captured instantaneously: sequential or interleaved slices are acquired across the entire Repetition Time (TR). Shifting each slice's time series to a common reference time aligns the hemodynamic response with the event design matrix.

equation.name: Power et al. (2012) Framewise Displacement (FD) & Volterra Expansion
equation.latex: \text{FD}_t = \underbrace{|\Delta d_{x,t}| + |\Delta d_{y,t}| + |\Delta d_{z,t}|}_{\text{Translational Step (mm)}} + \underbrace{R_{\text{arc}}\!\left(|\Delta\alpha_t| + |\Delta\beta_t| + |\Delta\gamma_t|\right)}_{\text{Rotational Arc Step at } R_{\text{arc}}=50\text{ mm}}, \qquad \mathbf{m}_{24}(t) = \big[\mathbf{m}_t, \mathbf{m}_{t-1}, \mathbf{m}_t^2, \mathbf{m}_{t-1}^2\big]
equation.summary: Combines frame-to-frame translational and rotational head movements into a single millimeter displacement index and expands motion into 24 nonlinear/delayed nuisance regressors.

terms.meaning: Sum of absolute frame-to-frame shifts (in mm) along the three Cartesian axes between volume t-1 and volume t.
terms.failure: Differencing cumulative position poorly or failing to set FD_0 = 0 at the first time point.

terms.meaning: Converts angular rotations (in radians) to millimeter displacement on a cortical sphere of radius R_arc = 50 mm.
terms.failure: Adding raw degrees or unscaled radians directly to millimeter translations without the 50 mm radius conversion.

terms.meaning: Includes current, 1-TR delayed, and squared motion terms to capture nonlinear partial-volume and T1 spin-history disturbances.
terms.failure: Assuming rigid realignment alone removes motion artifacts from functional connectivity.

PR10.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Rigid-Body Head Motion (6 DOF), Framewise Displacement (FD) & Spin-History Artifacts
online_diagram.guide: Head movement during an fMRI run is parameterized by 3 translations (x, y, z in mm) and 3 rotations (pitch, roll, yaw in radians). Even after rigid realignment puts the brain back on the grid, out-of-plane motion disrupts steady-state T1 longitudinal magnetization (spin-history artifacts).

equation.name: EPI Phase-Encoding Voxel Shift & Jacobian Pile-Up Correction
equation.latex: \Delta y_{\text{PE}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{\gamma \, \Delta B_0(\mathbf{x})}{\text{BW}_{\text{PE}}} = \gamma \, \Delta B_0(\mathbf{x}) \cdot T_{\text{readout}}, \qquad I_{\text{corr}}(\mathbf{x}) = I_{\text{dist}}\!\big(\mathbf{x} + \Delta y_{\text{PE}}(\mathbf{x})\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{PE}}\big) \cdot \left(1 + \frac{\partial \Delta y_{\text{PE}}}{\partial y_{\text{PE}}}\right)
equation.summary: Relates local magnetic field inhomogeneity Delta B0 to millimeter displacement along the phase-encoding axis and corrects compression pile-up via the 1D Jacobian.

terms.meaning: Off-resonance phase accumulated over the slow effective EPI readout time translates directly into spatial shift along the PE axis.
terms.failure: Applying unwarping along the frequency-encoding axis or reversing the PE polarity sign (+y vs. -y), doubling the distortion.

terms.meaning: Corrects artificial intensity brightening where multiple native voxels were compressed into one distorted voxel.
terms.failure: Shifting voxel positions without Jacobian scaling, leaving artificial hyperintensities in compressed frontal regions.

terms.meaning: Geometric unwarping moves surviving signal back to its true location, but cannot recreate signal destroyed by through-slice T2* dephasing.
terms.failure: Claiming fieldmap unwarping restored orbitofrontal/ventral temporal signal that had already dropped to the noise floor.

PR11.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Susceptibility Distortion Correction (SDC): Geometric Unwarping vs. Signal Dropout
online_diagram.guide: Air-tissue interfaces near the sinuses warp the static B0 field. Because EPI has tiny bandwidth along the phase-encoding (PE) axis, field offsets Delta B0 shift voxels by several millimeters along PE and pile/stretch intensities—while through-slice dephasing causes irreversible T2* signal dropout.

pipeline_steps: Convert to Physical Sigma & Voxel Sigma

equation.name: Gaussian Kernel FWHM Conversion & Anisotropic Voxel Scaling
equation.summary: Converts a user-specified Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM in mm) into the Gaussian standard deviation sigma in physical and per-axis voxel units.

terms.meaning: Exact ratio between the width where a Gaussian falls to 50% of its peak and its standard deviation sigma.
terms.failure: Passing FWHM directly into scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter(img, sigma=FWHM), over-smoothing by 2.35x in every dimension (13x in volume!).

terms.meaning: Divides physical millimeter sigma by each axis's voxel spacing Delta x_d so smoothing is isotropic in physical space.
terms.failure: Using a single scalar voxel sigma on anisotropic slices (e.g., 2x2x4 mm), blurring twice as far through-plane.

terms.meaning: Volumetric smoothing averages gray matter with adjacent CSF and white matter; masked or surface-based smoothing prevents cross-tissue bleed.
terms.failure: Smoothing before fine-grained MVPA/RSA or laminar analysis, destroying high-frequency spatial pattern information.

PR12.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Spatial Gaussian Smoothing, FWHM-to-Sigma Conversion & Boundary Bleed
online_diagram.guide: Convolving an image with an isotropic 3D Gaussian kernel suppresses high-frequency thermal noise and increases overlap across participants at the matched spatial scale (Matched Filter Theorem), but blurs signal across sulcal CSF boundaries and white matter.

pipeline_steps: Rasterize Stimulus on Sub-TR Grid dt

equation.name: Continuous Neural-to-BOLD HRF Convolution & Discrete Scan Sampling
equation.latex: x_c(t) = (s_c * h)(t) = \int_{0}^{\infty} s_c(t - \tau)\,h(\tau)\,d\tau, \qquad X_{n, c} = x_c\!\left(n\cdot\text{TR} + t_{\text{ref}}\right), \qquad h(\tau) = \frac{\tau^{a_1-1}e^{-\tau/b_1}}{\Gamma(a_1)b_1^{a_1}} - \frac{1}{c}\frac{\tau^{a_2-1}e^{-\tau/b_2}}{\Gamma(a_2)b_2^{a_2}}
equation.summary: Convolves the neural boxcar/stick stimulus train s_c(t) with the double-gamma hemodynamic impulse response h(tau) in continuous time, then samples at each volume acquisition timestamp.

terms.meaning: Indicator or parametric modulation train in seconds built from onset and duration columns of events.tsv.
terms.failure: Rounding event onsets to the nearest integer TR before convolution, destroying jittered event-related timing.

terms.meaning: Difference of a positive gamma peak (~5–6 s delay) and a smaller delayed undershoot gamma (~16 s delay), acting as a ~0.18 Hz low-pass filter.
terms.failure: Using closely spaced fixed-ISI trials without jitter, causing overlapping HRFs to merge into a flat constant.

terms.meaning: Samples the continuous convolved predictor at the exact reference timestamp of scan n (and truncates the tail to length N_scans).
terms.failure: Forgetting to slice np.convolve(s, h)[:N_scans], producing a design vector longer than the fMRI time series.

D05.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Block vs. Event-Related Designs, HRF Convolution & Sub-TR Microtime Sampling
online_diagram.guide: Neuronal events s(t) stored in BIDS events.tsv (onset and duration in seconds) pass through the sluggish canonical double-gamma Hemodynamic Response Function h(t) (peaking at ~5–6 s with a ~16 s undershoot). Convolving on a fine sub-TR microtime grid before sampling at slice acquisition times preserves sub-second onset precision.

pipeline_steps: Apply Zero-Phase Filter / DCT Drift Basis

equation.name: Nyquist Folding Frequency & Zero-Phase Butterworth Magnitude Response
equation.summary: Determines the highest unaliased frequency at sampling interval TR, predicts where fast cardiac/respiratory rhythms fold back, and characterizes zero-phase high-pass filtering.

terms.meaning: Maximum temporal frequency resolvable at sampling period TR (e.g., 0.25 Hz at TR=2.0 s; 0.625 Hz at TR=0.8 s).
terms.failure: Hardcoding TR=2.0 s in filter design when the actual dataset was acquired at TR=0.72 s.

terms.meaning: At long TR (e.g., 2.0 s), a 1.1 Hz cardiac pulse folds into 0.1 Hz—right inside the resting-state passband (0.01–0.10 Hz) where a bandpass filter cannot remove it.
terms.failure: Assuming a 0.01–0.10 Hz bandpass filter removes cardiac noise from slow-TR fMRI.

terms.meaning: Removing frequency bins restricts residual variance to a lower-dimensional subspace, reducing statistical degrees of freedom.
terms.failure: Computing t-statistics or correlations after aggressive bandpass filtering without adjusting effective degrees of freedom.

PR13.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Temporal Frequency Filtering, Nyquist Aliasing & Passband Degrees of Freedom
online_diagram.guide: Slow scanner drift (<0.01 Hz) and physiological pulsations (respiration ~0.3 Hz, cardiac ~1.0 Hz) contaminate fMRI time series. Designing a digital filter requires knowing the exact sampling period TR, checking whether cardiac frequencies alias into the passband, and reducing effective degrees of freedom.

equation.name: Joint Orthogonal Nuisance & Filter Subspace Projection
equation.summary: Projects the time series orthogonally onto the complement of the combined filter-and-nuisance column space in a single simultaneous linear operation.

terms.meaning: Concatenates motion expansions, anatomical WM/CSF PCA components, spike deltas, and frequency-filter bases into one design matrix.
terms.failure: Sequential modular denoising (filtering Y first, then regressing out unfiltered N), which re-introduces filtered noise frequencies.

terms.meaning: Annihilates all components of y lying in column space C(N); satisfies (P_N^perp)^2 = P_N^perp.
terms.failure: Subtracting non-orthogonalized nuisance fits sequentially, allowing shared variance to leak back in.

terms.meaning: Each linearly independent nuisance column consumes one temporal degree of freedom from the T time points.
terms.failure: Consuming >70% of temporal DOF with aggressive nuisance models without accounting for variance inflation.

PR14.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Nuisance Regression, Orthogonal Subspace Projection & Joint vs. Modular Denoising
online_diagram.guide: Denoising removes variance spanned by nuisance regressors N (motion, WM/CSF CompCor, ICA noise components). However, if you bandpass-filter the data and then regress out unfiltered nuisance columns sequentially, the nuisance step re-injects stopband frequencies into your cleaned time series (Lindquist et al., 2019)!

pipeline_steps: Audit Retained vs. Excluded Sample Bias

equation.name: One-Hot Spike Regression Censoring & Retained Effective Time
equation.summary: Zeroes the influence of C motion-corrupted volumes via one-hot delta columns while tracking remaining clean scan duration and sample selection bias.

terms.meaning: Root-mean-square frame-to-frame signal change across all in-brain voxels, indexing global intensity spikes alongside kinematic FD_t.
terms.failure: Checking only FD_t and missing non-kinematic coil spikes or delayed spin-history bursts.

terms.meaning: Indicator column with 1 at bad frame t_c and 0 elsewhere; absorbs 100% of frame t_c's residual without breaking uniform TR spacing.
terms.failure: Deleting rows from the 4D array before temporal filtering or AR(1) modeling, which stitches non-adjacent time points together.

terms.meaning: Total surviving seconds of clean data; participants falling below ~4–5 minutes have unstable connectivity estimates and must be flagged.
terms.failure: Retaining participants with 30 seconds of uncensored data, or ignoring that excluding high-motion participants systematically drops younger/clinical individuals.

PR15.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Quality Control (QC), Motion Scrubbing / Spike Censoring & Exclusion Bias
online_diagram.guide: High-motion frames (e.g., FD > 0.2 or 0.5 mm, high DVARS) cause distance-dependent functional connectivity artifacts. Censoring contaminated frames via one-hot spike regressors preserves temporal continuity, whereas naive array slicing before filtering corrupts temporal lag structure.

pipeline_steps: Fit K-Lag FIR Toeplitz Deconvolution Matrix

equation.name: Taylor Basis Expansion vs. Finite Impulse Response (FIR) Deconvolution
equation.latex: y(t) = \beta_1 (s * h)(t) + \beta_2 \left(s * \frac{\partial h}{\partial t}\right)\!(t) + \beta_3 \left(s * \frac{\partial h}{\partial w}\right)\!(t) + \varepsilon(t) \quad \text{vs.} \quad y_t = \sum_{k=0}^{K-1} \theta_k \, s_{t - k} + \varepsilon_t
equation.summary: Contrasts a 3-parameter Taylor expansion around the canonical HRF against a model-free K-bin Finite Impulse Response (FIR) lagged indicator basis.

terms.meaning: Linear combination with the temporal derivative captures small (+/- 1 s) onset latency shifts; combined magnitude is sign(beta_1)*sqrt(beta_1^2 + beta_2^2).
terms.failure: Adding the derivative to the GLM design matrix but testing only beta_1 at the group level, which still penalizes delayed regions.

terms.meaning: Estimates a separate free parameter theta_k at every post-stimulus time bin k=0..K-1 with zero parametric shape assumptions.
terms.failure: Using FIR on an unjittered periodic design where Toeplitz lag columns are collinear (rank-deficient).

terms.meaning: Canonical HRF has low variance (1 DOF) but high bias under latency shift; FIR has zero shape bias but K-fold higher parameter estimation variance.
terms.failure: Fitting a 12-bin FIR model to only a handful of trials without checking design conditioning.

D06.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: HRF Shape Misspecification: Canonical Basis Sets vs. Finite Impulse Response (FIR) Deconvolution
online_diagram.guide: Hemodynamic latency and dispersion vary across brain regions and age groups. If a region's true response peaks 2 seconds late, a rigid 1-column canonical HRF underestimates amplitude and spills structured waves into the residuals—whereas adding temporal/dispersion derivatives or a flexible FIR basis captures the true waveform.

pipeline_steps: Rotate DWIs by Rigid Matrix R
Rotate Gradient Vectors g' = R g

equation.name: Stejskal-Tanner Diffusion Attenuation & Gradient Rotation Rule
equation.summary: Links directional signal attenuation to the apparent diffusion coefficient along gradient g_k and enforces coupled rotation of image volumes and gradient vectors.

terms.meaning: Summarizes gradient strength G, pulse duration delta, and diffusion time Delta; b=0 is the non-diffusion-weighted T2 reference.
terms.failure: Treating b=5 s/mm^2 hardware crushers as heavy diffusion shells or failing to normalize by S0.

terms.meaning: Water diffusing rapidly parallel to white-matter axons (g_k || fiber) dephases strongly, producing dark signal and high ADC.
terms.failure: Reversing the physical interpretation and thinking bright DWI signal means high diffusivity.

terms.meaning: Applies the rotational component of the image alignment transform to each unit gradient vector in .bvec.
terms.failure: Rotating the 4D diffusion image volumes without rotating the .bvec table, misaligning all downstream fiber orientations.

PR16.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Diffusion MRI Stejskal-Tanner Gradients, b-Values & B-Table Rotation Invariance
online_diagram.guide: Diffusion MRI sensitizes each volume to water molecule Brownian motion along a specific unit gradient vector g_k = (g_x, g_y, g_z) at diffusion weighting b_k (s/mm^2). If you rotate a participant's head during motion correction or registration, you must apply the exact same 3x3 rotation R to the gradient table!

equation.name: Sequential Operator Non-Commutativity in dMRI Preprocessing
equation.summary: Demonstrates why Marchenko-Pastur PCA denoising and Gibbs unringing must precede spatial interpolation and eddy-current unwarping.

terms.meaning: Separates bulk Marchenko-Pastur random matrix noise eigenvalues from low-rank signal; requires spatially independent voxel noise.
terms.failure: Running eddy/interpolation before MP-PCA, which correlates neighboring voxel noise and breaks the Marchenko-Pastur eigenvalue bound.

terms.meaning: Removes sinc-oscillation ripples parallel to high-contrast CSF/white-matter boundaries via local subvoxel grid shifts.
terms.failure: Leaving Gibbs rings uncorrected, creating artificial low-FA/negative-diffusivity bands in the corpus callosum.

terms.meaning: Corrects gradient-direction-dependent eddy-current shears, head motion, slice dropout outliers, and susceptibility distortion in one resampling step.
terms.failure: Resampling separately at each substep, compounding spatial blurring.

PR17.phase: Phase III · Image Processing & Biophysical Pipelines

online_diagram.title: Diffusion Preprocessing Order: Thermal Denoising, Gibbs Unringing & Eddy-Current Correction
online_diagram.guide: Each dMRI artifact arises at a specific physical stage: thermal noise is independent in raw k-space/voxel space (MP-PCA), sharp skull/CSF edges truncated in k-space create oscillating Gibbs rings, and rapid diffusion gradients induce eddy-current shears. Interpolating before denoising correlations thermal noise across voxels and breaks MP-PCA!

pipeline_steps: Compute MD, AD, RD & FA Maps

equation.name: Diffusion Tensor Model, Mean Diffusivity (MD) & Fractional Anisotropy (FA)
equation.summary: Fits a 6-parameter symmetric diffusion tensor D to directional attenuations and summarizes its ellipsoid shape via Mean Diffusivity (trace/3) and normalized eigenvalue variance (FA).

terms.meaning: Projects the symmetric 3x3 tensor D=[Dxx,Dxy,Dxz; Dyx,Dyy,Dyz; Dzx,Dzy,Dzz] onto unit gradient direction g_k (noting off-diagonal factor-of-2 in the 6-column design matrix).
terms.failure: Omitting the factor of 2 on off-diagonal terms (2*gx*gy*Dxy) when constructing the linear least-squares design matrix.

terms.meaning: Average diffusivity across all three principal axes; elevated in CSF and chronic tissue loss, reduced in acute cytotoxic edema.
terms.failure: Allowing noise/Gibbs ringing to produce negative eigenvalues (lambda_3 < 0) without SPD projection.
